senses.gloss: (abbrev. of קאם, v. קָאֵים a. קוּם) [he, it stands,] a particle of emphasis, mostly untranslatable.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 2a:13">Ber. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>מכדי … אימת קא אכלי וכ׳</he> now, when do the priests eat T’rumah?; <he>מילתא … קא משמע לן</he> the Mishnah (in choosing that definition of the time) wants to teach us something else indirectly; <he>והא קמשמע לן</he> (abbr. <he>קמ״ל</he>) and it is this, it wants to teach us. Ib. 4ᵇ <he>והא דקא אמרי וכ׳</he> and the reason why they say &c.; a. v. fr.—V. <cite ref="S01437"><he>קָמָא</he> I</cite>, a. <cite ref="S00007"><he>קָאֵי</he></cite>.
